column1: # The routes and what must hold on each replay: tools/check_routes.py (ctest oracles-routes, with ORACLES_ROM_DIR set).

# castle-and-west.route with the objects' animation stepped from the fan game's tables (its manifest's six, bound where its bank-0 routines name them) against the live game (--object-animation-check): of the objects a neighbour animates by the rule (their code advancing their animation by one call of the step at each update of the capture's probe), the game's changes by its data are all the step's, the step's are the game's but those its NPCs' code chooses as Link comes near; the probe's verdict is never the other of the game's first updates after a scroll (none here with Link away); every pose shown live has its tiles in the capture.
# castle-and-west.route with the rooms never visited kept dark (--unvisited-rooms hidden): the game's record of the rooms entered on Gifts of Kinomi's profile.
# With the settling camera a dark room's pixels arrive once more before the band shows it bare: 7 edge fades (enhanced.edge_fades), the previous camera 8.

# castle-and-west.route with the transitions' diagonal (--continuous-diagonal): the scroll down into 0:14 leaves Link at the game's own distance, above the stairs the machine's last steps once pushed him onto (enhanced.scroll_solid_arrivals), stairs being walked on beyond it with --continuous-swim alone, which the fan games do not have; the game goes elsewhere from 3741 on, before the route's carries, and the diagonals held before then meet walls across (transitions.carry_withheld_frames).

# east-cave.route: from the castle's save, out of the castle and down the map's first rows to 0:37 on its east edge, into the cave there, 3:38 below 3:28, up and back, out and in again (recorded with the transitions' diagonal). The cave is two interior rooms joined by a scroll, which the drawn-back view shows in its whole band with the room it opens onto, as the rooms off the map, where it showed the normal band centred in its own, black around (enhanced.normal_band_frames, 609 frames before); the far view in 4:3, taller than two rooms, without a jump at the scroll's end. The camera's jump down is 5:b1's, as the game's file loads.

# The large room loads blank before the cave shows: its people, drawn beyond the game's window from their model, stay under its tiles with priority, as on the game's screen, rather than showing a frame over it (enhanced.sprite_hidden_frames).

# east-cave.route in the far view in 4:3, with the sub-pixel camera as without it: the band shows the cave's two rooms whole, and a scroll from one to the other changes the game's room at once; the camera follows Link through the scroll's start, where it was held at the camera of the frame before until the game's window moved and then jumped by the 10 to 12 pixels it had missed (enhanced.camera_jumps_y=2, the scroll's starts counted 36 frames instead of 17). Leaving the cave, the game in its room still, it is held as before (enhanced.alone_scroll_frames).

# The compact text (--text compact, Enhanced alone), Kinomi's English laid out again in the banks its profile leaves to a language and drawn by the transaction at the profile's routines: compact-castle-and-west.route, castle-and-west.route's keys with Link waiting from the frame the compact text closes its first dialogue to the frame the game's layout did (its comment), the same rooms at the same frames; the dialogue's lines in the font's own widths, none past 128 pixels, the reveal to the pixel (none cut or early), the box where the game drew it.
# castle-and-west.route with the status bar laid out (--hud wide): Gifts of Kinomi's bar is the base game's, laid out in every world frame.

# castle-and-west.route with Text size Large and Very large (--text-size, the counters of ages/checks.tsv): the game's box enlarged from the core's image, as in Ages and Seasons, on the 337 frames of a text; the box the host draws compared with the core's on each of them (--text-box-check); the live state that of its row without them.

# castle-and-west.route with the sub-pixel camera (--enhanced-subpixel), measured: the castle's large rooms (6 scrolls between them) and the diagonals walked there and outdoors (704 frames). Drawn at his exact place, Link on the ground no longer steps across then down in turn on a diagonal (enhanced.link_wobble, 204 without the option); the two left are the game's own steps, the first as a wall stops him across at the end of a diagonal in a large room (2812), the window of the measure still holding the diagonal.

# The wide text box (--text-box wide, the counters of ages/checks.tsv), Kinomi's English laid out again at 192 pixels, classic at the game's fixed advance and compact (text.boxes as the game lays them out, text.boxes_laid_out as served): each frame the box shows, its text against its layout's glyphs, none wrong, none uncovered, cut or early, none past 192 pixels. The route's keys depend on the pages: its first dialogue, eight pages classic and four compact, closes in fewer boxes and the replay goes its own way past it, the same on each, out of no room (transitions.taken).

# shop-wide.route: shop.route's keys for the wide text box (recorded with text-box-wide), the princess's dialogue closed 90 frames sooner as compact-castle-and-west.route, the same rooms to the shop (2:5e); its price's choice, OK or No thanks, the cursor moved to No thanks and back before the purchase. Kinomi's English laid out at 192 pixels (the counters of ages/checks.tsv); the fan games' engine draws the cursor in the line's tiles (text_box.cells, text_box.cursor_cells, the cell shown at each place the game's in the VRAM: text_box.cursor_pixels_wrong). With the compact text the shop's texts page otherwise and the replay leaves the village: no row.

# shop.route: castle-and-west.route's keys to the village (0:13), then by hand a bomb dropped (5160) and ten bombs bought for 20 rupees in its shop (2:5e); --poke-at gives Link, whose save has neither, five bombs on B and 50 rupees at 5150 (wInventoryB, wNumBombs, the bombs' obtained flag set beside the save's, wNumRupees). With --cheats ammo,rupees the bomb is kept (cheats.ammo_kept) and the purchase costs nothing; with --cheats no-damage,rupees the castle's three hits cost no heart and the purchase nothing (the bombs bought because the hearts the shop sells are refused at full health).
